bullets.text: Q3 CR 87.8, reflecting continued frequency decreases; Property CR 111.8 (YTD 114.8), improving from Q2 via reinsurance agreements despite adverse weather; Special Lines operated within CR targets.

Gallup engagement reached 73% (98th percentile among surveyed companies) with 3% actively disengaged; culture index score improved across all five questions; four D&I objectives guide efforts to reflect customers and people led.
Property catastrophe net loss and LAE reached $115M across six named storms, 13 wildfires, and Iowa derecho (YTD $392M); mobilized 900 catastrophe claims representatives across the country.
Companywide NPW +14% YOY for Q3; Commercial Lines reached all-time high NPW, surpassing $5B on a trailing 12-month basis; Special Lines grew considerably on new business acquisition.
Companywide PIF +11% YOY, led by Direct auto at 14%; auto PIFs crossed 16M; Robinsons bundled auto/property customers reached 1.5M; Commercial Lines PIFs reached an all-time high.
Lowered personal auto rates ~1% countrywide in Q3, totaling ~3% cumulative cuts since April; Property rates increased, with minimum deductible requirements expanded to 12 states with hail exposure.

Personal Lines YTD weather catastrophe claims rose 18%, with Q3 peril claims up 21% YOY; vehicle miles traveled rose early in Q3, impacting loss frequency, before metrics flattened in the second half.
Smart Haul surpassed $300M DPW on a trailing 12-month basis; Snapshot ProView live in 40 states; Lyft rideshare partnership expanded by four states and DC to eight total markets.
Portfolio total return was 1.7%, led by equities at 9.6%; valuations across equity and fixed income markets are no longer as attractive as during the March through June timeframe.

Transportation and contractor applications rebounded above pre-COVID trajectory, driven by high spot rates and strong housing starts; 'welcome back' program supported businesses with credits and favorable treatments.
